name: NAPALM
what_it_is: NAPALM (Network Automation and Programmability Abstraction Layer with Multivendor support) is a Python library providing a unified API to connect, configure, and retrieve operational state from network devices across multiple vendors. It abstracts vendor-specific CLIs and APIs behind a single interface.
components: vendor drivers (EOS, IOS, IOS-XR, JUNOS, NXOS, etc.)
napalm CLI tool (command-line client for get_facts and other getters)
measurement: get_facts (hostname, vendor, model, OS version, uptime, serial number, interface list)
modes: candidate config workflow (load → compare → commit or discard)
constraints: Requires Python 3.9 or later (as of version 5.1.0+)
Some NOS require feature pre-enablement: XML agent on IOS-XR, NXAPI on NXOS
Not all getter methods are implemented for all drivers — support matrix varies per vendor
Atomic replace vs merge semantics differ by platform; not all platforms support candidate configs
No built-in fault injection or traffic generation capabilities
Real or emulated network devices required — no built-in mock/simulation mode
notable_absences: No docker-compose file in the repository (neither main nor master branch)
No fault injection or chaos engineering features
No built-in traffic generation or measurement probes beyond ping/traceroute
No streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC) support in core library
